# Objective

For this investigation, you will explore how poverty and food-store access vary across counties in a US state of your choice. 
Each student must choose a different state, and California is reserved for the example. 

Use the California example to guide the appearance and organization of your results (I am not showing your my code).


# Wrangling the data

## Obtaining the data

1. Visit U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA's) [Food Environment Atlas ](https://ers.usda.gov/data-products/food-environment-atlas/data-access-and-documentation-downloads) and download the `Food Environment Atlas .csv Files` (current Version).

2. Move the 3 downloaded data files into your week 7 repo (two csv files and one txt file).

3. Open the `ReadMeFile2025.txt` and read it to learn about this data.


## Preparing your data

4. Notice I provided you with the code to read in and initially prepare your data. Remove `#| eval: false` from the provided chunk so it will run when you render your document. 

5. Run the provided code to import the data, clean the column names, and reshape the dataset. Examine both `usa_food_og` and `usa_food`; you will explain their differences in Reflection Q1.

6. Starting with usa_food, create a new object containing only the counties in your selected state. Give this object a descriptive name.

7. For your subsetted data, convert metro23 to a logical variable.

8. For your subsetted data, reorder the county factor by `pct_laccess_pop19`, the percentage of residents with low food-store access in 2019.

9. For your subsetted data, use `!ends_with("*")` with a `seelct()` to drop columns that are not for county level data.
